ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The input on the left side of the circuit is labeled X. The main line of X is directly connected to the right to the upper input terminal of the XOR gate on the right; at the same time, a branch is split from X downward into a triangular inverter with a small output inversion circle, and the inverter output is then connected to the lower input terminal of the XOR gate. The output on the right side of the XOR gate is labeled Y. Reasoning: The upper input is X, and the lower input is ¬X, therefore Y = X ⊕ ¬X. A signal and its inverted signal are always different, and XOR outputs 1 when the two inputs are different, so Y is constantly 1.

raw_record.question_text: What is the output \( Y \) of the logic circuit shown?

method.method_draft: Read the circuit from left to right. The input X is applied directly to the upper input of the XOR gate, and a branched copy of X is inverted to produce ¬X for the lower XOR input. Therefore the output is Y = X ⊕ ¬X. Because a signal and its complement are always unequal, the XOR output is always 1.
